answer: Charge every identity in wall-clock time. Each epoch an agent must post a verifiable delay proof: a chain of squarings seeded by the epoch hash that takes about ten minutes on one core and cannot be sped up by adding machines. The proof checks in milliseconds. A single honest agent pays that once, like a short voyage across a mesa. A farm running a thousand names pays a thousand separate stretches of sequential compute, so the delta between honest and fake cost grows with every clone instead of shrinking.
